4. Before discussing the indictments made against the appellant, we feel it necessary to describe the background of holding trial of the appellant. After creation of Pakistan, West Pakistani people started to look down the people of East Pakistan saying "a low-lying land of low lying people" who "polluted" the area with non-Muslim values. Bengalis were politically excluded as Pakistan was ruled by the Non-Bengali rulling elites who belonged to West Pakistan or military dictators from west Pakistan. East Pakistan was also economically exploited as resources were transferred from East to West Pakistan. After creation of Pakistan its people, for the first time, exercised their franchise for electing their representatives in the Parliament, both in National Assembly and Provincial Assembly for formation of Parliament and to run the Government by the representatives of the people of Pakistan. Results of the election held in 1970 were as under: 

 5. It is constitutional convention that the President shall request the majority party leader to form Government. But in case of Pakistan, the President did not request the majority party leader to form government. After publication of the result of parliamentary election, the events that took place in Pakistan were widely published in different Newspapers. Some of those news items are quoted below for perusing the actual situation prevailing in Pakistan: 

 7. Mr. Z.A. Bhutto, Chairman of the Pakistan People's Party, declared in Lahore on Sunday that no Constitution could be framed nor could any government at the Centre be run without his party's co-operation. The PPP, he added, was not prepared to occupy the Opposition Benches in the National Assembly. 

 10. He said that the PPP had won majority in the provincial Assemblies of Punjab and Sind and added that the real power of the Centre lay in these two provinces. No government at the Centre therefore could be run without the PPP's co-operation, he added. 

 12. Earlier, he explained how the PPP fought against the Ayub regime and what hardships it had to undergo in its struggle to overthrow dictatorship. In this connection he referred to the efforts of former President Ayub Khan to perpetuate himself in power by convening a Round-Table Conference with he said, was a clear conspiracy against the people of Pakistan. That was the reason, he explained, that the PPP had refused to participate in RTC because it was the game of Ayub Khan to remain in power by conceding the principle of parliamentary form of government. 

 17. He reiterated that no Central Government could either he formed or function without the co-operations and support of People's Party. 

 22. In reply the President said, "When he (Sheikh Mujib) comes and takes over I won't be there. It is going to be his Government soon." 

 63. The Awami League leader announced the closure of all Government, semi-Government offices in Bangla Desh and stoppage of all rents and taxes until the demands of the Bengalis were accepted. 

 83. The Awami League Chief, however, asked the people to be on guard against the "enemies who are amongst us" trying to create disturbances. He said they must maintain peace and discipline and added: "It is your responsibility to protect the non-Muslims and non-Bengalis". 

 86. Mian Nizamuddin Haider, MNA-elect and a leader of the Bahawalpur United Front, has expressed full support for the four demands put forth by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and urged the Government to accept them so that the present grave political crisis can be resolved. 

 88. Referring to Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's complaint that he had been completely neglected by the Government while taking important decisions was fully justified as he was the leader of the majority party in the country. "In the present circumstances he is the only man who can keep Pakistan together and I appeal to people to rally around Sheikh Mujibur Rahman" he said. 

 115. He said that if this was the position, he would have agreed to the six-point programme straight away and, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman "would have been happy to accommodate him in the Government". 

 121. Mian Tufail Mohammad, Acting "Amir" of the Jamaiat-i-Islami said in Lagore on Sunday that the setting up of two separate governments in the two Wings of the country would be a negation of the Legal Framework Order. 

 131. In fact he pointed out the demand of Mr. Bhutto for "division of power between the two Wings amounts to the division of the country". The PPP Chief wanted "two constitutions, two governments and two countries", he remarked. 

 137. In a statement, he said Mr. Bhutto stood fully exposed and so Mr. Abdul Qaiyum Khan, both were a great obstacle in the way of transfer of power to the people, both of them wanted commitments about their share in the Government before they lent support for the Constitution-making. 

 Secretary-General, National Awami Party Mali group) on Monday evening said it was must "imperative" that "a caretaker" government should be formed at the centre. 

 143. These circles maintained that in a democracy majority party alone had the right to form the government. 

 176. In a nutshell, those were the political situations of Pakistan prevailing at the relevant days. Now let us see the activities of the President of Pakistan and its army, who were paid by the people of both the wings of Pakistan, that is, people of Bangladesh as well. President of Pakistan directed people's servant Pakistan army to attack their own people on the night between 25th/26th March, 1971. The commander of Pakistan armed forces in East Pakistan, General Tikka Khan, was soon nicknamed "Butcher of Bengal" in both the Bengali and international media, led the genocide committed in Bangladesh in that fateful night. Operation searchlight began as massive massacre indiscriminately using artillery in urban areas, particularly, in Dhaka and Pakistan army killed thousands of People, members of Police forces, members of East Pakistan Rifles and students. Pakistani generals, having lost in election because of the Bengalis, started slaughtering with an intention of wholesale reduction in the population of East Pakistan so that it would no longer comprise a majority in Pakistan. Pakistani military attacks targeted the Bengali nationalists with a particular focus on selected groups such as the students, intellectuals and Hindu community. 

 Tasks: 1. Neutralise by disarming 2 and 10 East Bengal, H.Q. East Pakistan Rifles (2500), Reserve Police at Rajar Bagh (2000). 

 1. Disarm 1 East Bengal and Sector H.Q. East Pakistan Rifles and Reserve Police incl. Ansar weapons. 

 2. Disarm 3 East Bengal at Saidpur. 

 1. Disarm 4 East Bengal, Wing H.Q. East Pakistan Rifles, Reserve district Police. 

 1. Disarm E.B.R.C., 8 East Bengal, Section H.Q. East Pakistan Rifles, Reserve Police. 

 5. Liaise with Shaigri and Janjua (C.0.8 East Bengal) who have been instructed to take orders from you till arrival Iqbal Shafi. 

 6. If Shigri and Janjua feel sure about their outfits then do not disarm. In that case merely put in a road block to town from Cantt. by placing a Company in defensive position so that later E.B.R.C. and 8 East Bengal are blocked should they change their lyalities. 

 186. Those are the actions of Pakistan army admitted by their officer against the people of Pakistan. From the aforesaid description it is apparent that the same was a preplanned, preconcert and premeditated military actions against unarmed civilians of Bangladesh with an object to destroy the civilian population by the Pakistani Rulers and their army. The Pakistan army initiated a calculated and well co-ordinated attack on Bengalis across the country. Time magazine dubbed General Tikka Khan, the "Butcher of Bengal" for his role in operation searchlight. Now we shall describe the actual actions of the Pakistan army in the mother land of the appellant on and from 25th March 1971. 

 188. "On the night between 25/26th March, 1971, General Tikka struck peaceful night was turned into a time of wailing, crying and burning. General Tikka let loose everything at his disposal as if raiding an enemy not dealing with his own misguided and misled people. The military action was a display of stark cruelty more merciless than the massacres at Bukhara and Baghdad by Changiz Khan and Halaku Khan----. General Tikka resorted to the killing of civilians and a scorched earth policy. His orders to his troops were: "I want the land and not the people--- " Major General Farman had written in his table diary, "Green land of East Pakistan will be painted red." It was painted red by Bengali blood". (Niazi,- Betrayal East Pakistan). 

 196. Caught completely by surprise, some 200 students were killed in Iqbal Hall, headquarters of the militantly anti-government student's union, I was told. Two days later, bodies were still smouldering in burnt-out rooms, others were scattered outside, more floated in a nearby lake, an art student lay sprawled across his easel. 

 215. The troops stayed on in force in the old city until about 11 p.m. on the night of Friday, March 26, driving around with local Bengali informers. The soldiers would fire a flare and the informer would point out the houses of Awami League supporters. The house would then be destroyed- either with direct fire from tanks or recoilless rifles or with a can of gasoline, witness said. 

 216. Meanwhile, troops of the East Bengal Regiment in the suburbs started moving out towards the industrial areas about 10 miles from the Sheikh's centres of support. 

 218. One of the last targets was the daily Bengali Language paper "Ittefaq". More than 400 people reportedly had taken shelter in its offices when the fighting started. At 4 o'clock Friday afternoon, four tanks appeared in the road outside. By 4-30 the building was an inferno, witnesses said. By Saturday morning only the charred remains of a lot of corpses huddled in back rooms were left." 

 (a) Sadarghat is the dock area of old Dacca. On the morning of March 26U1 Army troops attacked the terminal. No civilians were armed in that area. A machine gun was installed on the terminal roof and all men, women and children were fired upon. Inspection of the terminal on March 29th revealed pools of dried blood on the terminal floor. The washrooms were completely soiled and soaked with blood. According to an eye-witness, A Bengali student, all civilians who were waiting for boats in the terminal were killed. After the massacre, bodies were dragged into buses and burned. Corpses were still floating in the Buriganga River adjacent to the terminal on March 29th. 

 (c) Home of Professor G.C. Dev. Head and Professor of Philosophy at Dacca University, was also attacked the same night. Professor Dev, a noted Bengali Hindu Philosopher, has never been politically involved. He was an elderly bachelor who housed poor students, often leading discussions about philosophy and religion. His home was attacked and all students were killed. Professor Dev himself was marched to the adjacent field and killed. 

 8. Professor Innasali, Head of Department of Physics, wounded. Other faculty members were also killed during the attack on the university, but their deaths could not be verified. Personal reports by wives of faculty members indicated that specific professors were sought by the army, especially those involved with Economics, Political Science and Bengali Culture. Although the exact circumstances of death are not known, one example has been pieced together by visits to faculty housing and eyewitness accounts from family members. On March 28th Building 34 contained pools of blood on the first and second floor foyers. According to wives of faculty members, troops attacked the building on the morning of March 26th. Apartment A was entered forcibly and the faculty member marched to the courtyard where he was shot. Fortunately he was only injured with a neck wound and was last known to be in critical condition at Dacca Medical College. The soldiers then went to Flat D, where Professor Muniruzaman lived. He, his son, brother who was an advocate on the East Pakistan High Court and the only son of his sister-in-law were marched to the first floor foyer, lined up against the wall and machine-gunned. The wife of Professor Zaman dragged her wounded husband back to their apartment, hiding him in the bed-room; Three hours later when the soldiers returned to remove the bodies they re-entered his apartment, again dragged him down the stairs and killed him. 

 (e)The British Council which is located near Dacca University was also attacked on the morning of March 26th. According to a British Council official, who was trapped in his home near the Council Building during the gunfire, the troops broke into the Council and destroyed some books because they mistook the Council for the University Library. In addition, eight Bengali local policemen who were stationed at the Council were killed during the surprise attack. This official's bedroom and house were subjected to machinegun fire during the entire night. Only after day break did he dare tell the soldiers that he was a British subject and they did not kill him. 

 (f) The east Pakistan Police barracks are located in Dacca. It housed approximately 5,000 policemen. On the morning of March 26th, it was attacked without warning by mortar, tanks and a large number of troops. Although there was resistance, most policemen were believed to be asleep when the attack occurred and to have died during the fighting. The barracks building were completely levelled by heavy arm fire and were gutted by fire. (g) East Pakistan Rifles (EPR) was formed as a native Bengali force to concentrate its efforts at border patrol. On the morning of March 26th the EPR barracks in Dhanmondi was attacked by a similarly equipped force. Once again the number of deaths is unknown, although reliable estimates indicated that approximately 1,000 EPR's were stationed in Dacca, Groups of EPR soldiers were seen by Americans being trucked away. The fate of these soldiers is unknown." 

 221. I saw many bodies floating down the Buriganga between May 6 and May 10. Their hands were tied together and in some cases six to seven victims had been roped together. There were no signs of violence on the bodies. Some people nearby told me that the victims were workers belonging to the Sattar match factory on the outskirts of Dacca and that non-Bengalis were responsible for the killings. But I have no proof of this. 

 222. "Mr. Hassan Ullah Chowdhury, the Manager of the Bengali edition PURAB DESH, was hacked to death two weeks ago by non-Bengalis in his house in Mirpur, nine miles out of Dacca. This is a non-Bengali residential area and most of the Bengalis were either attacked or killed there after the army took over. 

 223. On May 5, I was passing Nawabpur Road in the old area of Dacca. I saw three army trucks stop next to a group of Bihari Muslims. They pointed towards a Bengali at a nearby shop. A soldier lifted his rifle and shot the man without asking a question. 

 224. If they see any able-bodied Bengalis, they pick them up in a truck and takes them away. I don't know what happens to them. 

 07.04.1971. The New York Times Bloodbath in Bengal. 

 "---- On any basis, the United States would have a humanitarian duty to speak against bloodbath in Bengal". 

 "--- A New York Times correspondent, who crossed from India into East Pakistan, reported that government troops, acting on orders from Karachi, have killed engineers, doctors, professors and students in an attempt to eradicate the future Bengali leadership." 

 "Eyewitness reports, one more ghasty than another, continue to filter out of East Pakistan, telling of the massacre of the Bengali people by Pakistani Army evidence mounts that it is cold bloodeadly murdering minority Hindus. Bengali separatists, intellectuals, doctors, profes-sors, students, in short those who could lead a self governing East Pakistan". 

 02.08.1971. The Time Magazine. The Ravaging of Golden Bengal. "---- Kushtia a city of 40.00 now looks, as a world Bank team, reported, "like the morning after a nuclear attack" 

 "The official estimate of the West Pakistan Government is that only 15,000 have died, but the lowest independent estimates start at 100,000 and many estimates are over a million have died already." 

 April, 1971. Jhon Stonehouse's interview with B.B.C. "What happened in East Bengal "makes Vietnam look like a tea-party". 

 05.07.1971. The Stateman "British M.P. Arther Bottomley said this had been the most horrowing mission he had undertaken in his entire public life. Oxfam Report. The testimony of 60 on the crisis in Bengal. They are eye witnesses, and the story they tell is horrifying. It is a story of mil-lions hounded, homeless and dying. It is too a story of the world community engaged in a communal ostrict act". 

 Senator Edward Kenedy "The tragedy of East Bengal is not only a tragedy for Pakistan. It is not only a tragedy for India. It is 'a tragedy for the entire world community, and it is the responsibility of that community to act together to ease the crises" 

 Dr. R.C. Hioman, MRCP, Save the Children fund, Bengal. "Tens of thousands of children have already died in the refugee camps in the India border area". 

 P 190- Claude Azonlay, Paris Match. "The whole world stands accused of inaction while seven million people are in danger of death. A graveyard of children. In Bengal two million children are dying, killed by hanger, and we remain idle and no sanctions will be imposed on us except may be of so remote - that of guilt." 

 The blame for the catastrophe rightly enough belongs to the men who run the West Pakistan Government. The shame belongs to all of us. Almost from the start, the World community could have stopped it. And it must be stopped now by whatever manner or means. Our children will inherit enough shame." 

 John Drewary, Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. "1 found it impossible to shut away the memories of what I saw, in the refugee camps of west Bengal and along with trials leading out of East Pakistan, in that corner of my mind reserved for other horrors I witnessed during wards I covered in Korea, the Congo, Egypt, Vietnam and Biafra. It is not that the brutization of the people of East Pakistan is worse than what has happened to countless others throughout history. The effect of sword, fire and starvation differ very little in degree on the individual body and spirit. It is simply that the magnitude of the tragedy is so immense, so overwhelming, it overshadows all other things. The cry for help coming out of in and East Pakistan is echoing all around the world. If we ignore it we are killing our future too." 

 "We, the under signed scholars of Asian Studies on the faculty of UCLA write to express our profound sense of anguish and shock at the news we have read and personally received of the brutal and protracted massacres of Bengali civilians by West Pakistan's armed forces since March 25, 1971. From every creditable report we have seen it appears that General Yahya Khan's Army directed the full strength of its fire power at such bastions of "resistance" to his military dictatorship as the unarmed camp of Dacca University". 

 "Tragic incidents in East Pakistan. Mr. Saxbe, Mr. President, I invite the attention of Senators to further events and accounts relating to the tragic incidents in East Pakistan. Mr. Saxbe readout an articles published in the Boston Sunday Globe July 11, 1971. Title was: East Pakistan a mounting crisis- witness reports on Death, Destruction. 226. Pakistani Major General Khadim Hussain Raza wrote in his book that Niazi in presence of Bengali Officers would say "Main iss haramzdigom ki nasal badal doonal (I will change the race of the Bengalies)". A witness said"The troops used to say that when the commander (Lt. Gen. Niazi) was himself a raper, how would they be stopped?' 

 227. Professor Adam Jones, Professor, Political Science, University of British Colombia, Canada in his "The Bangladesh Genocide in Comparative Perspective" has said, "This despite the fact that from a comparative perspective, the Bangladesh Genocide of 1971 was one of the most extreme and destructive genocides of the twentieth century, with as many as 3 million people killed. Reading English language sources like Anthony Mascarenhas's short book and even Kalyan Choudhuri's impressive work "Genocide in Bangladesh" I was struck by the parallels between "Pakistani slaughter of Bengalies and some of the most savages atrocities in modern record, including the Christian in the Ottoman Empire during the first World War, Japanese rampages in China and the Nazi genocide in Eastern Europe during World War two. The scale and most emetic character of the slaughter and material destruction was simply breathtaking. 

 228. Those are pictures, in short, prevailing in the mother land of the appellant. Genocide, torture, murder, rape etc. were characteristic of Pakistani army. Pakistani attack targeting Bengali population was an attack on a specific ethnic group to suppress their hopes and aspirations, destroy their identity and eliminate their existence. It was an attack upon human diversity committed against Bengali nationalist group with the intent to destroy the very existence of the group. Those were widespread and systematic attacks against unarmed civilians committed by the Pakistan army in the name of Islam and United Pakistan though they knew very well that they themselves had killed Pakistan on the night of 25th March, 1971 by killing the countrymen. The world community shamefully failed to prevent the genocide committed in Bangladesh by the Pakistan army in 1971. 

 282. P.W.9 Mostafa Ali son of Victim Mazed Ali, in his testimony stated that, his father Mazed All had been serving as a security guard of Shaestaganj food godown it was his routine work to go to the food godown every day to provide lunch to his father. At about 11.00 a.m. on 29.04.1971, Mostafa Shaheed and others went to Shaestaganj food godown for taking delivery of food grains for the freedom fighters. He went there to give lunch to his father. At about 1.30 p.m. on 29.04.1971, at the time of loading food grains from food godown in a truck, Sayed Qaiser and 2/3 others rushed there by a jeep. He got down from the jeep and observed the act of loading food grain froth the godown. Thereafter, he left the place towards old market. Sometimes thereafter, members of "Peace Committee" and Pakistani army rushed there chanting "Pakistan 'Zindabad" slogan. Appellant Qaiser Ali entered into food godoWn and brought out the officers and staffs of food godown including the father of this wit-ness, Sub-Divisional Food Controller Abdul Aziz, Chief Inspector Abdul Khaleque, Officer-in-Charge of godown Rezaul Karim, security guards Abdur Rahman and Gedaulla and handling contractor Tara Miah . At that time, his younger brother (P.W.11) and this wit-ness were present inside the food godown. At one stage, appellant Qaiser wanted to know the particulars of the order giver of loading of food grains in the truck for the freedom fighters. Officer-in-Charge of the godown replied that Commandent Manik Chowdhury had sent his men for loading the food grains for taking delivery of the same for the freedom fighters. The appellant passed order not to load the food grains from the godown anymore and directed the officers and staffs to perform their duties accordingly. At about 10/10.30 a.m. on 29.05.1971, this witness came to know from his maternal uncle that the appellant and his bahini and Pak army again went to Shaestaganj food godown. Getting such information, this witness and his younger brother took shelter in a house situated near Shaestaganj food godown and saw that the Pakistan army, Qaiser bahini and the appellant Qaiser himself, confining his father and 7(seven) other officers and employees of food godown, were going towards Shaestaganj Dackbaglaw. This witness and his younger brother followed them hiding themselves. They found that those victims were kept confined in a room of the Dukbangalow. Appellant Qaiser was talking with the Pakistani army in the field of the said Dukbangalow. At about 2.00 to 2.30 p.m., they saw that the Pakistani army and the appellant and his bahini confining those victims, were going towards old bazaar of Shaestaganj. This witness and his brother (P.W.11) followed them hiding themselves. They found the members of Pak army and Qaiser bahini to pressurize the victims to stand up in a line near Railway bridge of river Khoai. The appellant gave signal to Pakistani army and then and there members of Pakistani army gunned down those 7(seven) victims including the father of this witness. This witness claimed that his younger brother (P.W.11) and he him-self saw the occurrence of brutal killing of their father. At that time of deposing, this witness became emotional in the dock. He further stated that earlier his father used to work with the father of the appellant Qaiser and nursed him in the days of his childhood. But he did not bother to kill his father. They threw the dead bodies of the victims in the river Khoai. The dead bodies of the victims were not recovered. In his cross examination, he stated that the distance between food godown of Shaestaganj and the Dukbangalow is less then 1/4th mile. On 29.04.1971, there is no boundary wall surrounding the food godown. Government quarters of Sub-Divisional food controller Abdul Aziz and Chief inspector Abdul Khaleque were situated at Habigonj town. But it was their routine work to inspect to food godown of Shaestaganj everyday since the same was the largest food godown at Habigonj. He denied the defence sugges-tion that the statements made in his examination in chief are not true. 

 304. In order to prove Charge No.8, the prosecution examined two witnesses, P.W.18 Basu Sautal and P.W. 20 Abdul Motaleb. Of them, P.W.18 stated that in the last part of Boishak, perhaps it was May, 11, 1971, his elder brother Bipin and he himself were staying in the house his Pishi (father's sister) at her dwelling hut. At that time his Pisha went outside the house. At about 10 a.m., after having breakfast, he was sitting in the courtyard and his Pishi was working in her kitchen. At that time, Gafur, Abdul Haque and two Pakistani army personnel entered into their house along with another Bengali man wearing civil dress. This witness took shelter behind a bush and saw that the civil dressed man gave signal to Pakistani army personnel to enter into the house of his Pisi. Accordingly, those two members of Pakistan army entered into the house of his Pishi Hiramony Sautal. Thereafter, his Pishi raised alarm seeking help to save her. His grandfather Bipin rushed there to rescue his Pishi but they resisted them. Gafur and Abdul Haque assaulted his grandfather who raised alarm. Thereafter, he did not hear any sound of his Pishi. This witness returned to the house after leaving Pakistan army personnel and those persons and found that Pakistan army had raped upon her Pishi. In the afternoon, local people went there and disclosed that the person wearing white print shirt was Qaiser Ali of village Nowapara. He denied the defence suggestion that it was not true that the occurrence did not take place in the manner stated above. 

 In 1965 War, Sher Bahadtir took shelter in his house. Thereafter, Pakistan army moved towardS Chandpur through their vehicle's taking the witness with them. Appellant Qaiser, Major Yousuf and some members of Pakistani army stopped their vehicles near Chandpur Chagolbazaar. Appellant Qaiser Ali and two other Bengalee and Pakistani army went to a tea garden. Then this witness asked Major Yousuf what he would do. Who rekliecr that he may leave the area. This witness took shelter in a sugarcane field situated behind the house of Hiramoni Sautal. He was not previously acquainted Hiramoni Sautal. He heard the sound of outcry from the house of Hiramoni Sautal. An old man tried to protect her. At that time, the appellant Qaiser and two other Bengalee people assaulted him. This witness went to the house of Hiramoni Sautal and found that she was crying. He came to know that Pakistani army, at the instance of appel-lant, entered in to the house of Hiramoni Sautal and raped upon her. In his cross examination, he denied that it is not true that in the War of 1965 Major Yousuf and Sher Bahadur took shelter in his house. 

 314. P.W.22 Md. Lokman Hossain was aged about 17 years in 1971. In his testimony, he stated that after having breakfast on 15th May, 1971 he went in search of his maternal uncle Abdul Jabbar near Primary school and found that Abdul Jabbar, keeping his cattle-head in the field, was running towards their village. This witness asked him about the cause of his running who replied that Pakistani army was coming towards their village. This witness returned to his house and found the villagers running towards Indian border. This witness took shelter beneath the heep of paddy straw situated at the south western corner of his house. He heard the sound of firing. He saw appellant Qaiser, some Bengalee and members of Pakistani army standing in front of the house of Abdul Gat/it They killed Gofur on the spot. At 1.30 p.m. Pakistani army left the village. Then this witness came out from the heap of paddy straw and saw the dead bodies of the victims. He visited the village and found P.W.21 Omar All and P.W. 17 Ful Miah. They buried those unfortunate victims. In his cross examination, he denied that appellant Qaiser was not present with the Pakistani army at the time of com-mission of the aforesaid occurrence. He also denied that the statements made above are not true. He also denied the defence suggestion that at the instance of Kazi Kabiruddin he has deposed falsely. 

 350. "Another pathetic case is that of a woman of about 25. I-Ter husband was a government officer in a Sub-division and she had three children. They first took away the husband, although she cried and pleaded with them. Then they returned him half-dead, after brutal torture. Then another lot of soldiers came in at 8 or 9 A.M. and raped her in front of her husband and children. They tied up the husband and hit the children when they cried. 

 386. "Let us now consider whether there is any direct involvement of the accused in support of the charge. It is to be noted that the incidents of offences of the nature have been perpetrated about 42 years before the trial has taken place. It is one of the challenging task to collect legal evidence because of the changes during this intervening period, but also the fact that most of the witnesses are not alive. More so, in the intervening period, the political scenario had been changed after the killing of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. The regime which came to power rehabilitated the anti-liberation forces and the persons who perpetrated these crimes against humanity were also accommodated in the government. Those perpetrators perpetrated crimes against humanity in a similar manner. They not only screen out the legal evidence but als6 distorted the history of the liberation struggle lest their abhorrent roles are known by the young generation. This has done by the defeatdd forces of the First World War and the Nazis in the second world wars, even thereafter, in Cambodia, Khemr Rouge regime of Polpot, Tatsis in Rwanda, Serbian forces in Bosnia etc. The court can take judicial notice of this common practice from the history. In our country the admitted position is that some right wing political parties with direct cooperation and participation of the perpetrators remained in power from 1975 and destroyed, destructed, and defaced almost all legal evidence in a planned manner. 

 389. From the facts, circumstances and evidence adduced by the prosecution it is proved that the appellant was involved in deliberate and systematic destruction and killing of unarmed Bengali civilians and was also involved in aiding, planning, contributing and abetting the Pakistan army who committed genocide and crimes against humanity with an object to wipeout in whole or in part of Bengali nation. 

 392. Out of the indictments brought against the appellant, the prosecution has been able to prove two charges in respect of crimes of rape and sexual violence. In ICT Act, 1973 includes rape as one of the components of crimes against humanity. Rape is a violent and torturous act that severs the personal dignity of victims in a humiliating and contemptuous manner. Rape and forced pregnancy are crimes against humanity and genocide as well since those involve the unlawful confinement of woman forcibly made pregnant which caused serious bodily and mental harm. The appellant had direct involvement of con-fining and abducting P.W.5 Majeda Begom and, thereafter, handing over her to Pakistan army. In spite of repeated request of her father and uncle he did not release Majeda. He knew very well about the fate of Majeda in army custody. He knew very well that Pakistan army dragged off thousands of such daughters of Bengal into sexual violence, rape and forced pregnancy which was crimes against humanity. 

 393. There have been hundreds of "Mylaies and Liddices" in Bangladesh due to the atrocities committed by Pakistan army. It was a tragedy for the entire world' community. The appellant himself was a witness of brutality and massacres of Bengali civilians committed by Pakistan army but without helping the helpless Bengalis he, forming a special bahini named "Qaiser bahini" participated in the crimes against Humanity and genocide and aided, abet-ted and facilitated the Pakistan army to commit such crimes. In Prosecutor V. Kamubanda, Case No. 1CTR-95-54-T-(Trial Chamber) it was observed that the principle that criminal responsibility for any crime in the statute is incurred not only by individuals who physically commit that crime, but also by individuals who participate in and contribute to the commission of a crime in other ways, ranging from its initial planning to its execution, as specified in the five categories of acts, namely, planning, instigating, ordering, committing or aiding and abetting. In the case of Semanza V. Prosecutor, Case No. ICTR-97-20A (Appeal Chamber), it was observed that for an accused to be convicted as perpetrator or co-perpetrator of genocide, it is not necessary that he or she fulfills a "key coordinating role" or that a "high level genocidal plan' be established even if the existence of a plan to commit genocide can be useful to prove the specific intent required for genocide. In the case of aiding and abetting no proof is required of the existence of a common concerted plan. No plan or agreement is required, indeed, the principal may not even know about the accomplice's contribution. The aider and abettor carries out acts specifically directed to assist, encourage or lend moral support to the perpetration of a certain specific crime and this support has a substantial effect upon the perpetration of the crime.
